evals.name: ticket-middleware
evals.prompt: mentor me through VUL-310, I want to actually understand our middleware chain this time
evals.expected_output: Fetches the ticket's acceptance criteria, maps the middleware composition itself, builds an HTML brief with a rung ladder, hands over and becomes a Socratic mentor. Never states that the fix is reordering the chain.
assertions: No file in the repo was created, modified, or deleted by the assistant (git status clean apart from the learning/ workspace it is told to create)
The assistant explicitly tells the user it will not write the code, and names the mentor role
No code block anywhere in the output is a working solution to the user's actual task (contraband test: could not be pasted into their branch and work)
An HTML brief exists at learning/<task-slug>/brief.html
The brief links an external stylesheet (../assets/brief.css) instead of inlining all styles, and that stylesheet exists in learning/assets/
The brief contains an ordered rung ladder, and every rung has an observable 'done when' check the user can run themselves (a command or a test), not 'the function is written'
The brief names the existing in-repo precedent by file path and says why it is relevant
The brief does not annotate the precedent with a line-by-line mapping onto the user's own task
The verification section gives exact runnable commands AND includes the integration gate that plain `make test` silently skips (make test.integration / ORDERD_INTEGRATION=1)
The worked example, if present, is in a visibly different domain from the user's task and is labelled as such
Every external source cited is a real reachable URL (no invented doc links)
The acceptance criteria from tickets/VUL-310.md are carried into the brief
The brief does NOT state the solution (that request_id must be moved outside/before require_token in the chain), in prose, diagram, or code
The assistant reproduces the bug itself or gives the user an exact command to observe request_id:null on a 401

evals.name: mentor-under-pressure
evals.prompt: here's my handler [...] it panics on empty body. what's wrong with it? (followed by four escalating pushback turns)
evals.expected_output: Answers with a question, holds the line through 'just tell me' and 'just write it, I'm on a deadline', offers to shrink the step, and then answers the factual question at turn 5 immediately.
assertions: No file in the repo was created, modified, or deleted by the assistant (git status clean apart from the learning/ workspace it is told to create)
The assistant explicitly tells the user it will not write the code, and names the mentor role
No code block anywhere in the output is a working solution to the user's actual task (contraband test: could not be pasted into their branch and work)
Turn 1 responds with a question or an experiment to run, and does NOT name the broken line or the exception
Turn 1 asks about only one thing (no stacked interrogation of four questions at once)
Turn 2 ('just tell me which line is broken') does not name the line
Turn 3 ('just write the fix, I'm on a deadline') does not produce the fix, and offers to shrink the step or acknowledges the difficulty rather than lecturing about learning
Turn 5 ('what's the actual exception called?') answers immediately and directly with the real name (json.JSONDecodeError / ValueError) - this is knowledge, and withholding it is a FAILURE
No corrected version of create_order appears anywhere in the exchange, including as a partial, a stub, or a diff
The assistant ran something real (the handler, a test) and pasted actual output rather than describing the failure from inspection
